scenario_detail.name: bulk_refactor
scenario_detail.note: Sixty files in one turn: twelve clean moves, four moves-with-rewrite, one module overwritten by a three-way split of a file that also moved, four unrelated new modules and four reformatted files. This is the size at which a quadratic candidate set starts to cost something, and at which one wrong pair in fifty is still a reviewer being lied to, so it prices both the cost bound and the precision bar.

scenario_detail.name: clean_moves
scenario_detail.note: Four byte-identical moves in one turn, then a turn that moves one file while editing another. Every detector must be perfect here; this is the case that prices the floor, and a detector that loses pairs here has a bug rather than a trade-off.

scenario_detail.name: conflict_merge
scenario_detail.note: One branch moves the file with no edit at all — R100 on the branch — while main rewrites it where it stands, and the reviewer resolving the conflict keeps the new path and finishes the rewrite. Reading the merge against its first parent, the deleted blob is main's rewrite and the added blob is the resolution, and they match only loosely. The same pair is trivial on one window and nearly hopeless on the next, which is the finding about *window choice* `e2.4` has to ship a decision for.

scenario_detail.name: copies_survive
scenario_detail.note: Two copies, one byte-identical and one edited, where the source file is never deleted. A rename detector cannot see a copy at all — no deletion pairs with the addition — and a content matcher widened to the whole tree to find them is exactly as likely to pair `admin.py` with `admin_v2.py`, which is a scaffold twin and not a copy. The copy case is where a wider candidate set is the point and the danger at once.

scenario_detail.name: cross_merge
scenario_detail.note: The move happens on a topic branch and reaches main inside a merge commit, and the merge is clean. Read against the first parent git calls it a rename at R100, so the interesting question is not the matcher at all: it is the walk. Under the shipped `MergePolicy::Skip` a merge contributes no file rows, and a first-parent walk never visits the topic commit, so whether a reviewer ever sees this move is a decision `e1.2` already made.

scenario_detail.name: evil_merge
scenario_detail.note: Two merges of the same shape, one clean and one evil. The evil one moves a file *inside the merge commit*: neither parent contains the destination path. That is what a conflict resolution that turns into a reorganisation looks like, and it is invisible to a spine that skips merges, which is the shipped default.

scenario_detail.name: generated_and_binary
scenario_detail.note: Three moves, two of which have no usable content evidence: a lockfile replaced by a different tool's lockfile at a different path, a byte-identical binary move (perfect content evidence, and the only case hashing alone solves), and a generated module regenerated at a new path with recognisably unrelated bytes. A spike that reports one number across these three is reporting nothing.

scenario_detail.name: merge_many_to_one
scenario_detail.note: Three deletions and one *modified* destination: `util/time.py` already existed and absorbed all three. Three pairs are true at once; a detector that emits one is wrong twice and missing once, and a reviewer told 'clock became util/time' will stop trusting the pane for the rest of the review.

scenario_detail.name: rebase_over_delete
scenario_detail.note: The branch moves a file main has deleted. The rebased commit contains an addition and no deletion at all: no window-local method — git's, a matcher's, or a human's reading of the diff — can recover the pair from the commit, because the source is not in it. The truth file marks this pair unrecoverable, and the report states the ceiling rather than scoring a method on a question it cannot ask.

scenario_detail.name: rebase_rewrites
scenario_detail.note: The move exists at `t1` and, after `git rebase main`, at a different commit under a different SHA with different parents. A reviewer's ledger and Fathom's episode identity both have to survive that; here the question is narrower and sharper — does the *pairing* come out the same on both sides of the rewrite? If it does not, the same episode changes its answer when the branch moves, which is worse than a missing pair.

scenario_detail.name: rebase_squash
scenario_detail.note: Pre-squash the reviewer saw two commits: a move at R100 and an edit to the moved file. Squashed — which is what `rebase -i` and every 'squash before merge' button produces — the one commit's window holds a move with most of the file replaced. The pairing is the same pair, and it falls off git's cliff between the two histories. A ledger that recorded it as a fact before the squash has to be able to be wrong after it.

scenario_detail.name: reformat_then_delayed
scenario_detail.note: Two turns of noise and one delayed move. The formatter pass is a change with no move in it at all, and the second turn is half noise and half a real move — the case where a rename detector and a noise detector disagree about who owns the file. Any pairing asserted on the reformat turn is fabricated out of whitespace.

scenario_detail.name: rename_rewrite
scenario_detail.note: Five renames, graded by how much of the file survived: a light edit, a medium edit, most of it replaced, all but the header replaced, and nothing but a shared header left. By author intent all five are renames. The last two are the ones no content algorithm can honestly call a rename — a reviewer staring at the two blobs cannot tell them from an unrelated new file either — which is what makes this the fixture that decides fact versus guess.

scenario_detail.name: scaffold_decoys
scenario_detail.note: One turn, two deletions, two additions. The true pair (`invoices.py` to `billing.py`) was rewritten on the way and carries weak evidence; the false pair (`orders.py` to `quotes.py`, and `orders.py` to `billing.py`) is scaffold overlap, which is large, stable, and has nothing to do with provenance. This fixture is not about recall: it is the manufactured ranking inversion the ticket asks about, where a wrong pairing outscores a right one.

scenario_detail.name: split_episode_move
scenario_detail.note: One turn, two commits: the old path dies in the first and the new one is born in the second. No commit-pair window contains both halves, so per-commit detection cannot produce this pair at any threshold, while the episode window sees it at R100. It is the cleanest evidence in the set that the *unit* of rename detection is a decision, not a detail.

scenario_detail.name: split_one_to_many
scenario_detail.note: One file becomes three, twice; the second split also adds code that never existed in the source. A 1:1 pairing can report at most one of the three destinations and silently drops the rest, so this is the fixture that forces the representation question `e2.4`'s second acceptance criterion is about.

environment.profile: prototype floor: Python, one process, git's CLI as gix's stand-in

at the shipped default git drops exactly one claimable rewrite, the one that lost half its lines
loosening to -M40 does not recover it: the bar is not the lever, the evidence is
git reports no split at all: a 1-to-3 split is structurally outside its output
a content matcher reports all six split pairs, which no 1:1 assignment can
git reports no fold-into-existing-module either: the destination is a modification and never appears in the additions
widening the destination set to modified paths is what makes a fold reportable at all
a copy whose source stays put is invisible to git at its default
--find-copies-harder buys both copies and one lie about a scaffold twin
and the lie is the named decoy, shipped as a 64% copy
widening sources to the whole tree is the only way to see a copy at all
and it pays for them with two further pairings that are not pairings

a conflict-resolved merge halves the same pair's evidence, and -M50 still clears it
and at -M75 the same true pair is gone: whether a fact is a fact depends on which window you measured it from
the evil merge's move is a pair git sees perfectly once the window exists
and a clean merge of a content edit produces no pair to argue about
a two-commit episode's move is invisible in the first commit
and invisible in the second: no commit-pair window contains both halves
and trivially visible when the turn is read as one window
a rebase does not change the pairing
a squash rebase drops the same pair below git's default bar
the same engine at a tenth still surfaces it, past the claimable line: the bar moved and the evidence really did collapse
a move rebased onto a history where the source was deleted cannot be recovered at any threshold, and nothing is claimed about it
git at its default asserts the scaffold decoy at R064 and misses the real rewrite at R015: the shipped floor is where the lie enters
a content matcher ranks the same decoy top of the window at J~0.49 while the true pair sits at J~0.06: the ranking is inverted, not mistuned
path similarity alone asserts two scaffold decoys at a score that looks like content evidence and is not any
a window in which nothing moved stays silent for every window-local configuration
the whole-tree widening manufactures four pairings among files that were merely edited in place, at scores a threshold can sit above

at the fact bar that pair is simply gone, which is what silence costs and what it buys
git lies about none of a 60-file refactor: every pairing it reports is true
and misses exactly the split parts of it
the hybrid at a 0.3 bar carries the fold and the split as well as git's own pairs

path similarity blended at 0.15 is the largest single source of wrong pairings in the table: the same matcher at the same bar goes from this many wrong to that many
MinHash changes a threshold decision at every boundary the product might pick: a 128-permutation sketch is not decision-preserving
git's similarity index is a badly calibrated confidence once the engine is allowed to pair anything (ECE at -M5)
the fixture set contains merge commits and history that was rewritten
the operating point with the lowest total harm in the whole sweep ships a named decoy: the cheapest answer overall is not one a reviewer can be given
a fact tier exists at all: some window-local bar ships nothing but true pairings
and it is not the cheapest point: refusing the decoy costs recall, measured as the gap in missed pairs
git's lie about the scaffold twin survives raising its bar to 0.60: the bar is not the problem, the pair's own score is
and the matcher's version of the same lie survives 0.45 — the false pair sits in the middle of the informative band, which is why no threshold can be the fact boundary
the deepest bar that adds a pair without meeting the decoy clears the false pair by less than two hundredths of a similarity point: that is a razor's edge, not a margin
the chosen fact tier ships nothing but true pairings on this corpus
the widest band worth showing is a trade of at least ten true pairs for one lie, and that ratio is what the display has to carry rather than a threshold

not_measured: real repositories: every number here is hand-authored content, so absolute rates are calibrated by shape and not by any corpus's popularity

whitespace-insensitive matching as a help: git-whitespace is identical to git-M50 on this corpus because every authored edit changed tokens, not indentation; a corpus of gofmt runs would read differently
gix's rewriter specifically: the git rows are git's CLI, which is the same algorithm's reference implementation, but a gix defect would not show up here
non-text payloads beyond one binary blob, and any language-aware similarity
the display cost of a guess tier: what a reviewer does with an uncertain pairing is e5.1's question, not this one

cheapest_band_all_told.note: the widest band worth showing, with its lies counted in the open: this is the trade the display has to carry, because no threshold closes it

deepest_without_a_known_false_pair.note: how far the bar can drop before a pair the truth names as not-a-move enters the shipped set, and what dropping it is worth on the way down

price_of_the_fact_tier.note: what refusing to ship a pairing you cannot stand behind costs, in pairs

rule.named_decoy_policy: zero tolerance for a *fact*; a guess band is defined by its label because no threshold removes the decoy from it
rule.objective: minimise weighted errors (wrong x 3, missed x 1), then maximise recall, then prefer the stricter bar
rule.scope_policy: window-local only: e2.4's own cost criterion excludes O(repo) candidate sets

spike.question: How often does each pairing method assert something untrue, and at what confidence is a pairing safe to show a reviewer as a fact?
spike.title: Spike: rename and copy detection reliability across merges
